sources.title: John Guy, Lost Kingdoms: Hindu-Buddhist Sculpture of Early Southeast Asia (2014), Kedah discussion
sources.note: Original museum catalogue indexed printed page20 read. Used Yijing 671 journey via Srivijaya/Kacha and Sungai Mas6th-11 thcentury range. Existing Dvaravati wheel passage from same whole volume counted cumulatively. Not adopted disputed Chitu=Kedah, exact foreign warehouse reconstruction or Tarumanagara conquest certainty.

sources.title: George Cœdès, Les inscriptions malaises de Çrīvijaya (1930), Talang Tuwo edition
sources.note: Original scholarly edition visually read pp38-41, including p39 transliteration and pp40-41 French translation. Persée page only yields first page; downloaded same article from http://sealang.net/oldmalay/archives/coedes1930etudes.pdf and rendered pages. Local coedes 1930.pdf and PNG witnesses preserved in parent folder. Single-work budget includes all reused parts; no modernized script invented.

sources.title: Directorate of Cultural Protection, Zonasi Kawasan Percandian Dieng (2020)
sources.note: Original heritage page full indexed text read; direct open failed. Temple phases late7th-early8 thcentury and through 780, ancient drains, nineteenth-century flooding/recovery. Avoided claim 808 is earliest Old Javanese inscription; dated 808 record used only as later local continuity.

sources.title: Nuratikah Abu Bakar and colleagues, The Development of Local Technology in Sungai Mas, Kedah from the 5th to the 10th Century AD (2018)
sources.note: Original author study read directly, pp 993-994/PDF4-5: brick/clay comparisons, stages, granite water jar and foot-washing interpretation, makara7th-9 thcentury. Excluded errors in general history/geography and unsupported superiority/origin claims. Jar belongs to sanctuary complex; no exact dated domestic sanitation inference.

sources.title: Zuliskandar Ramli and colleagues, Compositional Analysis of Sungai Mas, Kuala Selinsing and Santubong Glass Beads (2017)
sources.note: Original journal abstract read; volume17.2 is 2017, platform upload 2023 not original study date. Used glass lumps/compositional contrast to Indian glass as evidence for local bead manufacture. Confused site names in final dating sentence not repeated. Separate study from runtime 2011 XRF paper.

sources.title: Balai Pelestarian Kebudayaan Wilayah V, Prasasti Kedukan Bukit (2017)
sources.note: Original government heritage page full indexed translation read. Dates 682, boats and walking party, provisions, wanua. Direct fetch failed. Avoids contested numerical readings and precise geographic identification of Minanga; no unsupported single foundation claim.

sources.title: Bangka Regency Culture and Tourism Office, Prasasti Kota Kapur
sources.note: Original regional culture source indexed full text read. Ten lines, reading orientation, Pallava-type script/Old Malay,686 campaign and oaths. Historical exact calendar conversion not used; does not identify Bhumi Jawa with one securely conquered polity.

proposedOverrides.name: Early maritime Southeast Asian states
proposedOverrides.summary: A maritime Southeast Asian atlas umbrella for 600-800, covering different ports and communities connected through trade, religion and locally adapted writing.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Standalone 600-800 maritime umbrella; no sharing with later 800-1279 minor-hindu-and-buddhist-states
batchIdentityNotes.sites: Kedah/Palembang/KotaKapur/Dieng inside. Batujaya andBorobudur test outside; no archaeological comparison at those sites imported into this card.
batchIdentityNotes.limits: Not an Indian colony or uniform faith. Named Srivijaya and Mataram histories stay separate. TalangTuwo wishes show aspirations and hierarchy, not proven social outcomes. Shrine jar/ancient channels do not establish domestic plumbing.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: niyur (coconut palm), Old Malay transliteration directly inspected in Coedes 1930 pp39-40; original inscription 684. No guessed Pallava original characters.
